questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: determine concentration from ion-selective electrode potential
questions.stem: Sample 3201: An ion-selective electrode with slope 59.16 mV per decade reads 37.3 mV lower for an unknown than for a 4.83e-3 M standard. What is the unknown concentration?

options.misconception: treats the potential ratio as a concentration multiplier
ignores the potential difference and reports the standard concentration
applies the potential shift in the wrong direction

questions.explanation: The potential difference corresponds to a decade change equal to the shift divided by the slope. A lower potential for a cation means lower activity, so the concentration is the standard times ten to the negative shift over slope. Reversing the sign increases instead of decreasing concentration.
questions.hint: A decade is 59.16 mV for a monovalent ion.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: explain the basis of polarographic current
questions.stem: Measurement 3202: In polarography, what does the limiting diffusion current depend on?

options.text: It equals the charge passed during electrolysis of the entire solution
options.misconception: confuses a steady current with exhaustive coulometry

options.text: It is independent of concentration once a voltage is applied
options.misconception: mistakes a limiting current for a concentration-independent signal

options.text: It is set only by the reference electrode potential
options.misconception: confuses the excitation potential with the measured current

options.text: It is proportional to the concentration of the electroactive analyte under diffusion-controlled conditions

questions.explanation: When the applied potential is sufficient to reduce the analyte at the electrode surface, the current is limited by how fast analyte diffuses to that surface. That diffusion flux scales with bulk concentration, which is the basis for quantitative polarography.
questions.hint: Diffusion supplies the analyte to the electrode.

questions.stem: Observation 3296: In polarography, what does the limiting diffusion current depend on?

options.text: It equals the charge passed during electrolysis of the entire solution
options.misconception: confuses a steady current with exhaustive coulometry

options.text: It is proportional to the concentration of the electroactive analyte under diffusion-controlled conditions
It is set only by the reference electrode potential
options.misconception: confuses the excitation potential with the measured current

options.text: It is independent of concentration once a voltage is applied
options.misconception: mistakes a limiting current for a concentration-independent signal

questions.explanation: When the applied potential is sufficient to reduce the analyte at the electrode surface, the current is limited by how fast analyte diffuses to that surface. That diffusion flux scales with bulk concentration, which is the basis for quantitative polarography.
questions.hint: Diffusion supplies the analyte to the electrode.

questions.learningObjective: determine concentration from ion-selective electrode potential
questions.stem: Sample 3297: An ion-selective electrode with slope 59.16 mV per decade reads 93.8 mV lower for an unknown than for a 8.70e-3 M standard. What is the unknown concentration?

options.misconception: ignores the potential difference and reports the standard concentration
applies the potential shift in the wrong direction
treats the potential ratio as a concentration multiplier

questions.explanation: The potential difference corresponds to a decade change equal to the shift divided by the slope. A lower potential for a cation means lower activity, so the concentration is the standard times ten to the negative shift over slope. Reversing the sign increases instead of decreasing concentration.
questions.hint: A decade is 59.16 mV for a monovalent ion.
